How many Lucid Trading evaluation and funded accounts one trader can have active at the same time, and how the limit applies across product lines.

A
Written by AJ
August 26, 2026

Lucid Trading offers several account types, each designed to support a different phase of the trader’s journey. Below are the rules and limitations associated with each account type.

 

Evaluation Accounts

Account Limit: Up to 10 active evaluation accounts per household or family.

Shared Limit: Traders may hold a maximum of 10 accounts in total across evaluation accounts and funded accounts.

Example: If you have 5 evaluation accounts, you may only hold 5 funded accounts.

Reserve Limit: You may keep 5 evaluation accounts in reserve while you have 5 funded accounts.

You may trade evaluation accounts while they are in reserve.

Funded Accounts

Account Limit: Up to 5 active funded accounts per household or family.

Shared Limit: Different types of funded accounts combined may not exceed 5 accounts total.

Example: If you have 3 LucidDirect accounts, you may only maintain 2 LucidPro funded accounts.

Live Account

Account Limit: Up to 5 active LucidLive accounts per household or family.

O
Written by Operations Lead
October 20, 2026
LucidFlex Customization
Overview

LucidFlex gives traders the ability to customize their account at the time of purchase. Two settings can be adjusted to create the trading experience that best fits your risk preferences. The customization options are:

Daily Loss Limit: On or Off

Consistency: 40% or 50%

These settings create four unique LucidFlex account configurations.

 

Daily Loss Limit

The Daily Loss Limit (DLL) determines whether a daily loss cap is enforced on your account. The DLL is a soft breach, so if you hit it you will simply be locked out until the next trading session.

 

Daily Loss Limit On

A Daily Loss Limit is enforced on both evaluation and funded accounts

Results in a lower evaluation purchase price

Your funded account gets On Demand Payouts (see below)

Daily Loss Limit Off

No Daily Loss Limit is applied during either the evaluation or funded phase

Results in a higher evaluation purchase price

Payouts follow the regular end-of-day schedule

Consistency

40% (standard): your largest day must be 40% or less of your evaluation profit. Lowest price.

50% (add-on): your largest day can be up to 50%, so you can pass in as few as 2 days. Added at checkout for a small fee.

Consistency applies to the evaluation only. Funded LucidFlex accounts have no consistency rule. See LucidFlex Consistency Percentage.

On Demand Payouts

Keep the Daily Loss Limit On and your funded account can request payouts during the trading session, from profit made that session (6:00 PM to 3:45 PM ET).

After requesting an intraday payout, trading on your funded LucidFlex account is paused until the end of the trading day.

Accounts with a Hedging Violation are not eligible for intraday payouts. See Prohibited: Hedging.

With the Daily Loss Limit Off, payouts follow the regular end-of-day schedule.

Available Account Configurations

LucidFlex offers four possible combinations.

 

Option 1: Daily Loss Limit ON + 40% Consistency

Daily Loss Limit enabled for evaluation and funded

On Demand Payouts

Cheapest version of LucidFlex

Option 2: Daily Loss Limit ON + 50% Consistency

Daily Loss Limit enabled for evaluation and funded

On Demand Payouts

Pass in as few as 2 days

Option 3: Daily Loss Limit OFF + 40% Consistency

No Daily Loss Limit

Regular end-of-day payouts

Option 4: Daily Loss Limit OFF + 50% Consistency

No Daily Loss Limit

Regular end-of-day payouts

Pass in as few as 2 days

Highest pricing version of LucidFlex

Choosing the Right Configuration

Your customization should reflect your priorities:

Choose Daily Loss Limit ON if you prefer a lower purchase price and On Demand Payouts

Choose Daily Loss Limit OFF if you want more flexibility and don't mind paying a premium for it

Choose 50% Consistency if you want to pass faster

Once selected, these settings cannot be changed for an active account. If you want a different configuration, you'll need to purchase a new LucidFlex account with your preferred options.

LucidFlex Consistency Percentage

How the LucidFlex consistency rule works: 40% standard, 50% with the add-on, the calculation, and what it means for passing.

O
Written by Operations Lead
October 19, 2026
Consistency

The Consistency Percentage tracks a traders ability to earn profits over multiple sessions. This demonstrates a that a trader has and can adhere to a risk management strategy.

 

The Calculation

In LucidFlex evaluation accounts your Consistency Percentage must be 40% or less to be eligible to upgrade to a LucidFlex funded account. If you added the 50% consistency add-on at checkout, it must be 50% or less.

Use the following formula to determine if you are adhering to the Consistency Percentage:

 

Largest Single Day Profit / Account Profit = Consistency Percentage

 

Example

You trade your $50k LucidFlex evaluation account and your Largest Single Day Profit was $750 when you reached the $3,000 profit target. Plug the values into the above formula.

 

$750 / $3,000 = 25%

 

Congratulations, you are under the 40% requirement (and the 50% add-on). You may now upgrade to a LucidFlex funded account. If your largest day had been more than your limit (40%, or 50% with the add-on), you would keep trading until your largest day is back within it.

 

Cushion with the 50% Add-on

There is a small cushion built into the 50% consistency add-on so that traders that are super eager to pass in two days can do so. However, taking your time to reach your profit target is the best approach.

Overview

LucidDaily gives traders the ability to customize their account at the time of purchase. Two settings can be adjusted to create the trading experience that best fits your risk preferences. The three customization options are:

Daily Loss Limit: On or Off

Evaluation Drawdown: End-of-Day (EOD) or Intraday

Consistency: 30%, 40% or 50%

These settings create unique LucidDaily account configurations to suit the trader.

 

Daily Loss Limit

The Daily Loss Limit (DLL) determines whether a daily loss cap is enforced on your account. The DLL is a soft breach, so if you hit it you will simply be locked out until the next trading session.

 

Daily Loss Limit Enabled

A Daily Loss Limit is enforced on both evaluation and funded accounts

Results in a lower evaluation purchase price

Daily Loss Limit Disabled

No Daily Loss Limit is applied during either the evaluation or funded phase

Results in a higher evaluation purchase price

Consistency

30% (add-on): your largest day must be 30% or less of your evaluation profit. This is optional for accounts that use End-of-Day Drawdown in both the evaluation and funded stage to reduce the evaluation price.

40% (standard): your largest day must be 40% or less of your evaluation profit. Mid tier price.

50% (add-on): your largest day can be up to 50%, so you can pass in as few as 2 days. Added at checkout for a small fee. This is not available if the Funded stage has End-of-Day Drawdown enabled.

On Demand Payouts

With the Daily Loss Limit On, you can request payouts from your funded LucidDaily account during the trading session as soon as your dashboard shows all payout objectives are complete.

You can submit multiple payout requests from the same account within a single session, provided all payout requirements are met for each request.

Accounts with a News Trading Violation, or Hedging Violation, are not eligible for intraday payouts. See Prohibited: Hedging.

With the Daily Loss Limit Off, payouts follow the regular end-of-day schedule.

Evaluation Drawdown

This setting determines how the Max Loss Limit is calculated during the evaluation stage. If intraday drawdown is selected in the evaluation stage, this carries through to the Funded stage. 
​

Funded Drawdown

This setting determines how the Max Loss Limit is calculated during the funded stage. If End-of-Day (EOD) Drawdown is selected in the evaluation stage, the drawdown type in the funded stage can also be customized, between Intraday and EOD. 

 

End-of-Day (EOD) Drawdown

Drawdown is calculated using your account balance at the end of each trading session

Unrealized gains and losses do not affect the drawdown calculation

Results in a higher evaluation purchase price

Intraday Drawdown

Drawdown is monitored continuously throughout the trading session

Unrealized profits and losses are included in the calculation

Results in a lower evaluation purchase price

Available Account Configurations

LucidDaily offers many possible combinations, below are four examples:

 

Option 1: Daily Loss Limit ON + Intraday Evaluation Drawdown

Daily Loss Limit enabled

Evaluation uses Intraday Drawdown

Funded account uses Intraday Drawdown

Choice of 40% or 50% Consistency

Cheapest version of LucidDaily

 

Option 2: Daily Loss Limit ON + End-of-Day Evaluation Drawdown

Daily Loss Limit enabled

Evaluation uses End-of-Day Drawdown

Funded account uses Intraday Drawdown

Choice of 40% or 50% Consistency

Mid-tier pricing version of LucidDaily

 

Option 3: Daily Loss Limit OFF + Intraday Evaluation Drawdown

No Daily Loss Limit

Evaluation uses Intraday Drawdown

Funded account uses Intraday Drawdown

Choice of 40% or 50% Consistency

Mid-tier pricing version of LucidDaily

 

Option 4: Daily Loss Limit OFF + End-of-Day Evaluation + End-of-Day Funded Drawdown

No Daily Loss Limit

Evaluation uses End-of-Day Drawdown

Funded account uses End-of-Day Drawdown

Choice of 30% or 40% Consistency

Most expensive version of LucidDaily

 

Choosing the Right Configuration

Your LucidDaily customization should reflect your priorities:

Choose Daily Loss Limit ON if you prefer a lower purchase price and access to on-demand payouts on your funded account.

Choose Daily Loss Limit OFF if you prefer no daily loss cap and don’t mind paying a higher purchase price.

Choose Intraday Drawdown in Eval and funded for a lower evaluation purchase price.

Choose EOD Drawdown in Eval and funded if you prefer drawdown calculated at the end of the trading session and don’t mind paying a higher purchase price.

Choose 50% Consistency if you want to pass faster

Once selected, these settings cannot be changed for an active account. If you want a different configuration, you'll need to purchase a new LucidDaily account with your preferred options.

What Is It?

A trader goes long on one NQ in one account and short NQ on another. No matter which way the market moves, one account gains while the other loses, manipulating the program structure to secure profits unfairly.

 

Prohibited Forms of Hedging

Lucid Trading strictly prohibits all forms of hedging, including but not limited to:

Hedging across multiple accounts held by the same user

Hedging between different users' accounts

Hedging between different firms or funded platforms

Any other form of hedging designed to bypass risk management rules

What Happens If I Hedge?

Lucid Trading has automated risk systems in place to detect hedging behavior. If your account is flagged:

You will receive an email notice & the associated accounts will be reset to prior days balance. Despite the balance reset, this does not reset the total remaining drawdown on these accounts.

After repeated offenses all involved accounts will be breached and you may be permanently restricted from using Lucid Trading services.

Why Is It Prohibited?

Lucid Trading is committed to funding skilled, consistent traders, not those exploiting structural loopholes. Hedging:

Misrepresents a trader’s actual risk and skill

Undermines the evaluation process

Threatens the long-term sustainability of the firm

Allowing hedging would make it impossible to identify and reward legitimate trading performance.

Can I go long X contract and short X contract?

Can I go long X contract and short Y contract?

However, you cannot go long / short different contracts in separate accounts with correlated assets. This is strictly prohibited.
